GRU4Rec’s max losses normalize softmax weights over negative candidates only: BPR-max is −log Σⱼwⱼσ(s₊−sⱼ) + λΣⱼwⱼsⱼ²; TOP1-max is Σⱼwⱼ[σ(sⱼ−s₊)+σ(sⱼ²)]. Neither adds another division by negative count. Sampled cross entropy normalizes over the positive plus sampled candidates; sampling correction and label smoothing depend on the implementation. Candidate membership therefore changes the objective, including score regularization. [Paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf), [reference implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec/blob/master/gru4rec.py).

For matched-supervision experiments, the implementation implication is to distinguish retained query rows from candidate columns. Use identical retained targets, candidate IDs/multiplicities, sampling corrections and weighting in both context conditions. Removing a timestep’s own loss need not remove its target from other rows’ negative pools; filtering flattened examples before constructing in-batch negatives changes cross-example coupling. Compute each retained row’s complete loss, including score penalties, then apply the intended reduction: a token mean divides by retained valid targets; equal-user weighting requires per-user means first. Preserve explicit parameter regularization or optimizer weight decay separately. Full-context prefix states should remain differentiable through retained suffix losses; detaching them also changes gradient reach.

Once the baseline is supplied, check reduction axes, positive-index remapping, padding and duplicate-target handling, candidate masks before softmax/logsumexp, empty-negative rows, and all-masked batches. Verify that masking cannot produce 0×NaN, dropped query rows receive no direct score gradient, retained rows retain candidate-side gradients, and dense versus gathered implementations match losses and gradients on a tiny fixed batch. For left padding, read the final nonpadding position; confirm cropping preserves target alignment.
